```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Preface

The goal of this script is to conduct a WGCNA. The assumed working directory is the project directory. There are arbitrary decisions that must be made when running this analysis so the widget that created this script is initializing the environment you will need to run the chunks below. We have included information that may be useful for determining the cut-offs, but please be aware that there is some discretion about what is a "good" cut-off. We provide here our suggestions, but please consider your decisions thoroughly.

```{r}
library(DESeq2)
library(magrittr)
library(WGCNA)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(limma)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
```

## Initialize Environment
```{r}
genecountdir = "{directory containing STAR output}"
read1suffix = "{suffix that is part of read 1}"
meta_table = "{path to metadata}"
```

## Normalize Reads
WGCNA requires normalized reads. Here, we use DESeq2's vst function. Other options like TPM may also be suitable. 

```{r}
### Build gene counts dataframe ###
filelist = list.files(genecountdir, pattern = "*ReadsPerGene.out.tab")

#read in sample mapping dataframe
samplemap = read.table(file.path(dirname(genecountdir), "/sample_name_map.tsv"),
                        sep = "\t",
                        header = FALSE)
samplemap$V1 = unlist(lapply(samplemap$V1, function(x) basename(x)))
samplemap$V2 = NULL
samplemap$V3 = unlist(lapply(samplemap$V3, function(x) basename(x)))
samplemap$V4 = NULL

samplemap$V1 = unlist(lapply(samplemap$V1, function(x) sub(paste(read1suffix, ".fastq.gz", sep = ""), "", x, fixed = TRUE)))
samplemap$V3 = unlist(lapply(samplemap$V3, function(x) sub("_1.fastq.gz", "", x, fixed = TRUE)))

colnames(samplemap) = c("sample_name", "new_sample_name")

#initialize counts dataframe by reading in first file
counts = read.table(paste(genecountdir, "/", filelist[1], sep = ""))
row.names(counts) = counts$V1
counts = counts[,c(1, strandcolumn)]
colnames(counts)[2] = filelist[1]
counts[,3:(length(filelist)+1)] = NA
counts$V1 = NULL

for (i in 2:length(filelist)) {
    tempdf = read.table(paste(genecountdir, "/", filelist[i], sep = ""))
    counts[,i] = tempdf[,strandcolumn]
    colnames(counts)[i] = filelist[i]
}

colnames(counts) = lapply(colnames(counts), function(x) basename(x))
colnames(counts) = lapply(colnames(counts), function(x) sub("ReadsPerGene.out.tab", "", x))
cat("Read counts have been read.\n")

### Build metadata dataframe ###
meta_df = read.csv(meta_table, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

colnames(meta_df) = c("sample_name", "group_id")

meta_df = merge(meta_df, samplemap, by = "sample_name")
meta_df$sample_name = NULL
meta_df = meta_df[,c("new_sample_name", "group_id")]
colnames(meta_df)[1] = "sample_name"

row.names(meta_df) = meta_df$sample_name

### Prepare dataframes for input into DESeq2 ###
#put metadata in order of column names from gene counts matrix
all(rownames(meta_df) %in% colnames(counts)) #check all samples are in counts
all(rownames(meta_df) == colnames(counts)) #check samples are in order
counts = counts[, rownames(meta_df)] #put data in same order if the first is true but the second is false

#remove STAR info about unmapped, multimapped etc. reads
counts = counts[5:dim(counts)[1],]

#order factor levels for DESeq to know which is the reference group
group1_order = c(args$group1, args$group2)
meta_df$group_id = factor(meta_df$group_id, levels = group1_order)

cat("Metadata has been read.\n")

#load data in to DESeq object
dds = DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts,
                                    colData = meta_df,
                                    design = ~group_id
                                    )

#remove low count reads (optional, but I'm doing it)
keep = rowSums(counts(dds)) >= 10
dds = dds[keep,]

### Transform data for variance stabilization ###
vsd = vst(dds, blind = FALSE) #if setting `blind = TRUE`, within-group variability is calculated across ALL samples rather than within groups

#transpose for wgcna (rows = samples, genes = columns)
wgcna_input = as.data.frame(t(assay(vsd)))
```

## Outlier Removal and Quality Control

```{r}
#Find genes and samples with a lot of missing values or zero-variance
gsg = goodSamplesGenes(wgcna_input, verbose = 3)

if (!gsg$allOK) {
    #remove bad samples and genes
    filt_input = wgcna_input[gsg$goodSamples, gsg$goodGenes]
}

#It is also recommended to remove outlier samples based on clustering. We leave this decision to the user.
sample_clust = hclust(dist(filt_input), method = "average")
plot(sample_clust, sub="", xlab="", cex.lab = 1.5)

#If a sample looks like an outlier, you can remove it by uncommenting here and replacing `{OUTLIER}` with that sample's name.
#filt_input = filt_input[-which(rownames(filt_input) == {OUTLIER}),]
```

## Choosing beta (soft-threshold power)
WGCNA wants to achieve a scale-free topology pattern. This requires identifying a power (beta) that is used to transform the correlation matrix.
The choice of beta will shape the identification of modules.

```{r}
#If you think the default betas of 1-20 are too low, you can create a vector of powers you want to try with the `powerVector` kwarg
soft_threshold = pickSoftThreshold(filt_input,
    dataIsExpr = TRUE,
    corFnc = cor, #the correlation function
    networkType = "signed"
)

#Let's visualize model fit to identify an appropriate beta. We first need to convert the outputs into a signed R-squared
soft_threshold_df = data.frame(soft_threshold$fitIndices) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model_fit = -sign(slope) * SFT.R.sq)

#the recommended WGCNA model_fit cutoff is 80%
#if multiple values are above 0.8, you want to pick the one at the inflection point like when it starts to dip again 
ggplot(soft_threshold_df, aes(x = Power, y = model_fit, label = Power)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_text(nudge_y = 0.05) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, color = "#d78028") +
    xlab("Soft Threshold (Power)") +
    ylab("Scaled-Free Model Fit (signed R-squared)") +
    theme_classic()
```

## WGCNA
This will take some time when running. Grab a coffee. You deserve it.

`maxBlockSize` can be increased based on how much RAM you have available. You can approximate it as:
`maxBlockSize = (sqrt(RAM in GB)/2) * 10000`
```{r}
chosen_power = #the soft-threshold picked based on the graph above.

bwnet = blockwiseModules (filt_input,
    maxBlockSize = 15000,
    TOMType = "signed",
    power = chosen_power,
    numericLabels = TRUE, #Use numbers instead of colors for module labels. I find this easier than trying to distinguish literal shades of brown
    randomSeed = 42 #the data can be a little random, so setting a seed is useful to compare runs 
)

#That was a lot of hard work! To not have to run the above again, we can save the output to disk.
write_rds(bwnet,file = "../processed_data/WGCNA_output.RDS")
```

## Exploring modules
```{r}
#This will produce a dataframe with samples as rows and module IDs as columns. Values in the matrix are the "collapsed, combined, and normalized expression of the genes that make up each module"
module_eigengenes = bwnet$MEs

#Are samples still in order?
all.equal(meta_df$sample_name, rownames(module_eigengenes))

#This should be TRUE, otherwise you need to match the orders

#Create the design that the comparisons will be made on (i.e., the model with your predictor variable)
design_matrix = model.matrix(~meta_df$group_id)

#run linear models with each module as a response
model_fit = lmFit(t(module_eigengenes, design = design_matrix))

#smooth standard errors using empirical Bayes
smooth_model = eBayes(model_fit)

#multiple test correction and statistics extraction
model_stats = topTable(smooth_model, number = ncol(module_eigengenes)) %>%
    rownames_to_column("module")
```

`model_stats` is a dataframe in which every module has its own row with the log fold change in combined expression between groups, the Average Expression, the t-statistic, unadjusted p-value, adjusted p-value, and the log odds that the module is differentially expressed (B).

## Matching genes to modules

```{r}
gene_module_key = enframe(bwnet$colors, name = "gene", value = "module") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(module = paste0("ME", module))
```
